name: Cush
overview: Cush is a male biblical figure identified as the son of Ham, according to Genesis 10:6. There is no additional tribal affiliation or specific notes recorded about him beyond this lineage. His identity is primarily established through his paternal connection to Ham.
namesAndTitles: The name Cush appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:6. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is provided in the text, so it is presented plainly without additional interpretive significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Cush as the son of Ham and the father of several sons: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, Sabteca, and Nimrod. These relationships are explicitly detailed in Genesis 10:7-8, highlighting Cush's role as a progenitor of notable descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Cush's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his position within the genealogy of the nations, serving as a link between Ham and his notable descendants. Through Cush, the biblical record traces the origins of several peoples and individuals, including Nimrod, a figure associated with early leadership and kingdom-building. This genealogy underscores God's sovereign orchestration of human history and the fulfillment of His purposes through successive generations.
